claims.exact_statement: Let U(x,y) be C2 and scalar, with a unique smooth equilibrium minimizer y*(x) for each controlled deformation x and positive-definite U_yy. The reduced equilibrium response f(x)=+/- grad F(x), F(x)=U(x,y*(x)), has symmetric tangent K_eff=U_xx-U_xy U_yy^{-1} U_yx and zero work on every closed quasistatic x-cycle. The same conclusion holds for differentiable equilibrium Helmholtz free energy and for frictionless contact when all internal coordinates are included in a single-valued constrained energy minimization.
assumptions: all internal mechanical/contact states are included in y
the material is in equilibrium at each x and returns to the same full state
a scalar stored energy or equilibrium free energy exists
the reduced state is unique and smooth for the displayed tangent formula; nonsmooth contact transitions retain a single-valued reduced potential
no externally powered, chemical, thermal-gradient, or other work port is omitted
source_pointers: Derivation is included in the report; it follows from the envelope theorem and the Schur complement of the Hessian of U.
The 2023 target paper itself states reversible isothermal delta W=d psi in PDF p.13, lines 1491-1510.
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard reciprocity/thermodynamic integrability result; no novelty or priority claim. It excludes only source-free equilibrated models within the listed assumptions, not all passive viscoelastic or driven systems.

costs.theorem: No oracle or computation; model requires the complete internal state and potential.
costs.physical_test: Two-coordinate actuation, all boundary force/torque sensing, internal-state/contact imaging, and synchronized work integration.

claims.falsifier: A repeatable nonzero closed-cycle output with complete internal-state return and every mechanical, electrical, thermal, chemical, and other source port measured would contradict at least one stated physical premise or the theorem.
claims.next_gate: Independently audit force/coordinate conjugacy and all ports in the target finite-element model, then test a specimen under repeated cycles.

claims.exact_statement: Shaat and Park (JMPS 171 (2023) 105163) simultaneously state that every reversible isothermal increment obeys delta W=d psi and that the specimen returns to its initial state, while claiming a nonzero closed-cycle integral of delta W. Under those stated premises, integration forces the cycle work to be zero; the claimed nonzero value cannot follow unless a premise, state-closure assertion, or work accounting is changed.
assumptions: the paper's Eq. (31) applies to each increment of the claimed cycle
psi is a state function and the final full state equals the initial state
delta W is the same cumulative external work used in the later closed-cycle claim
source_pointers: PDF pp. 13-14, lines 1491-1538: Eq. (31), state-function closure, and claimed nonzero work.
PDF pp. 23-25, lines 2640-2712: FE energy balance claim, zero endpoint energy/displacements, and accumulated-work calculation.
PDF pp. 6-7, lines 586-625: rigid circles, elastic ligaments, frictionless normal contact description.
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a scoped audit of the cited paper, not an independent reproduction, formal peer review, or proof that every possible physical implementation fails. No priority claim is made.

costs.source_audit: Read the cited source pages; no new physical experiment performed.
costs.missing_evidence: Raw Abaqus reaction, couple, contact, force-work, and internal-energy outputs were not available in the retrieved record.

claims.falsifier: The audit is defeated if a consistent reinterpretation shows Eq. (31) or the state-return assertion does not apply to the same work and cycle, or if omitted ports/state changes reconcile the reported energy ledger.
claims.next_gate: Acquire the raw simulation output or author clarification and recompute work from all conjugate ports and full-state trajectories.

claims.exact_statement: For a postulated constant two-coordinate constitutive matrix K and a closed strain path of oriented area A, signed work is W=(K21-K12)A=2 kappa A, where kappa=(K21-K12)/2. A repeatable powered device with work-like drive delivering W_out per cycle of period T must receive drive work at least W_out plus dissipative losses each cycle; therefore P_drive >= W_out/T + P_loss. Thermal drive must be compared through available free energy (exergy), not raw heat. Without replenishment, a finite available-free-energy reservoir B obeys N W_out <= B over N cycles, before losses.
assumptions: linear constant constitutive response over the tested range
x_1 and x_2 are conjugate deformation/load coordinates
the full device is in a periodic steady state for the powered bound
the source term in P_drive is work-like energy; heat-driven cycles require an exergy balance
W_out is positive delivered mechanical work and P_loss is separately measured
source_pointers: Nature Communications 2021 paper derives odd-modulus work proportional to strain-space area and reports a piezoelectric/circuit-driven metamaterial.
Rahimi and Park 2026 preprint uses periodic driving of chiral gears and reports an effective odd shear modulus.
claims.novelty_boundary: Area-work identity and first-law accounting are standard. They are used here as an explicit cost equation for comparing powered dynamic structures with claimed source-free materials.

costs.measurement: Integrate load-cell force times displacement, torque times angle, electrical voltage times current, and chemical work ports over each period. For heat-driven cycles, meter heat and reservoir temperatures to compute available exergy.
costs.uncertainty: For exact displacement samples, force error epsilon_f, path length L, maximum sample step h, and force Lipschitz bound M_f, left-Riemann work error is at most epsilon_f L + M_f h L/2; other sensor and synchronization errors must be added.

claims.falsifier: A calibrated, closed, periodic device output exceeding the sum of all measured replenished input work and any reduction in stored free energy would contradict the full-system energy balance or indicate an unmeasured port.
claims.next_gate: Measure all mechanical and nonmechanical input ports on the driven specimen and report net useful output, heat, cycle time, reset cost, and cycle drift.
